title: compression plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `compression` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component CompressionConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

CompressionConfig.description: Plugin: compression — Null or an empty object uses defaults. On-the-fly HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 response compression (gzip, Brotli, and opt-in zstd) and optional request decompression. Process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_GZIP_ENABLED and FERRUM_COMPRESSION_BROTLI_ENABLED gates intersect with every instance and default to true; an instance with no remaining usable algorithm after those gates fails admission. Gzip/Brotli codec CPU is offloaded via a bounded spawn_blocking admission pool acquired only immediately before the blocking worker, while response buffering for compression is admitted by an independent bounded response-buffer semaphore reserved in before_proxy and held across the encode (with ineligible owners leaving the slot on the context for sibling handoff), so a slow backend cannot starve request decompression; authenticated /metrics exports ferrum_compression_codec_{admitted,saturated,join_failures,worker_failures}_total and ferrum_compression_response_buffer_{admitted,saturated}_total. Encode abort after a committed Content-Encoding restores identity headers on shared buffered H1/H2/H3 paths when identity remains acceptable, or replaces the response with 406 when the client excluded identity, rather than emitting mislabeled or explicitly refused plaintext. Optional request decompression parses Content-Encoding as an ordered coding list (OWS-tolerant), decodes supported chains in reverse order under hard-capped size/amplification limits, and fails closed on malformed/unsupported members. That decode runs on the shared strict, budget-charged decoder: br refuses Large Window Brotli, and the decoder's own heap plus every output growth (and, on a stacked chain, the previous pass's still-resident buffer) is reserved against FERRUM_REQUEST_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES before allocation, so an aggregate-budget refusal is a gateway 503 rather than a client 400. Normalization happens exactly once per request on every frontend: H1/H2 dispatch now receives the ownership context the native H3 path always had, so an already-normalized upload is never decoded a second time. Content negotiation follows RFC 9110 §12.5.3, treats x-gzip as the gzip compatibility token, strictly parses qvalues, and includes the identity coding: an uncoded response is acceptable by default at q=1 unless refused with `identity;q=0` or `*;q=0` without a more-specific identity entry (a nonzero wildcard does not lower identity quality), the most preferred acceptable representation wins (server preference order breaks ties toward compression), and the response is rejected with 406 when identity is unacceptable and no acceptable coded representation can be produced — including size/content-type ineligibility, identity range/delta responses (206/226, Content-Range, or the internal range marker), and `response_caching` HIT paths. That refusal is taken only after every effective instance in the chain has declined, so an earlier instance whose algorithms or content_types cannot serve this response never pre-empts a later sibling that can, and a committed coding is never turned back into a 406. Identity range/delta responses are non-transformable (forwarded unchanged when identity is acceptable); no-body statuses and already-encoded upstream responses remain protocol hard skips. Reject-path 406 replacement is scoped to cache HITs so auth/policy rejection statuses are not masked. Negotiation reads the client's own Accept-Encoding captured at request init, so a request_transformer rule that rewrites or removes the backend-facing header cannot select a coding the client refused or erase an identity;q=0. Honors request/response Cache-Control: no-transform and strong ETag validators by skipping compression (still 406 when that leaves no acceptable representation), unless weaken_strong_etag opts into compressing with a weak validator. When FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES (or the route ceiling) is unlimited or above 32 MiB, compression is length-gated: only a response whose backend declares a Content-Length within min(32 MiB, the buffered-response fallback) is buffered and encoded, other responses stream identity (406 when identity is refused), and plugin construction logs a warning. A later hook relabeling a committed Content-Encoding to a coding the instance cannot produce aborts the encode to identity (or 406). Unknown top-level keys are rejected at construction (for example `min_content_lenght` or `gzip_leveel`). Invalid generations fail file/admin/database/CP-DP admission while KeepLastKnownGood retains the prior published instance. Response buffering is only forced for responses this instance could actually encode: already-encoded origin responses and responses whose known Content-Length is below min_content_length stream instead of being collected. Multiple effective instances compose with first-wins ownership: the first instance that claims a supported request Content-Encoding owns strip+decode exactly once; the first instance that commits a gateway response Content-Encoding owns the single coding layer. Siblings must not delete the owner's request marker or compress again. An earlier identity/Vary-only decision does not block a later compress. H1/H2 and native H3 share the same sequential transform loops; reload snapshots remain atomic. WebSocket, gRPC message compression, and raw stream compression are separate protocol mechanisms.

algorithms.description: Enabled compression algorithms in server preference order (ties in client q-value go to the earlier entry). `zstd` (RFC 9659) is opt-in and never part of the default; it has no process-wide gate, and listing it also enables zstd request decompression when decompress_request is true. Each algorithm may appear once (`brotli` is an alias of `br`, so the pair is a repeat and is rejected at construction). An empty array is rejected at construction, as is an array left with no usable codec after the process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_* gates. Null selects the default.

min_content_length.description: Skip compression for bodies smaller than this (bytes). Must be an unsigned 64-bit integer that also fits usize on this host. Null selects the default.

content_types.description: Content-type whitelist (at most 64 rules). Defaults to 10 common text/application types. Every entry must be a bare ASCII type/subtype media type, or a type/* range covering every subtype of one top-level type, with no surrounding whitespace and no parameters; an empty array, an empty entry, a non-ASCII entry, a parameter-bearing or whitespace-only entry, any other `*` (*/*, */json, application/vnd.*+json), and a repeat of an earlier entry (compared case-insensitively) are all rejected at construction, because the matcher could never equal such a rule. Explicit null is rejected (unlike the other optional fields) — omit the key for the defaults. Matched as an exact media-type token (before the first semicolon, ASCII case-insensitive), or by top-level type for a type/* rule; response parameters like ; charset=utf-8 are ignored. Substring matching is not used, so application/jsonp does not match application/json.

max_decompressed_request_size.description: Zip bomb protection: max decompressed request body size in bytes (default 10 MiB). Hard-capped at 32 MiB; when request decompression is enabled, it must also be ≤ FERRUM_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_SIZE_BYTES if that wire limit is set. Per-layer/cumulative decode ceilings and a 1024:1 raw-to-decoded amplification bound apply, and the decode's complete working set (strict decoder heap plus output capacity) is charged to FERRUM_REQUEST_DECODE_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES before allocation — a budget refusal is the gateway capacity terminal (503), not a 400. Null selects the default.

remove_accept_encoding.description: Strip Accept-Encoding from backend request so backend sends uncompressed. Only applied when the instance still has at least one usable response codec after process-wide FERRUM_COMPRESSION_* gates. Null selects the default.

gzip_level.description: Gzip compression level (0=no compression, emits gzip framing only; 1=fastest, 9=best). Null selects the default.

brotli_quality.description: Brotli quality (0=fastest, 11=best). Null selects the default.

zstd_level.description: Zstandard compression level for the opt-in `zstd` algorithm (1=fastest, 19=best). Capped at 19 because higher levels use a window above the 8 MB RFC 9659 allows for the zstd content coding. Null selects the default.

weaken_strong_etag.description: Opt-in. When false (default), a response carrying a strong ETag is never compressed, so the validator is preserved. When true, such a response is compressed and the coded variant carries the weak form of the validator (W/"…"); an origin weak validator is kept as is, and an aborted encode restores the origin validator on the identity body. An ETag with no weak form (unquoted, list-valued, or containing invalid characters) and a strong ETag a later hook adds still keep the response uncoded. Null selects the default.

decompress_request.description: Enable decompression of gzip/brotli request Content-Encoding lists (plus zstd when `algorithms` lists it; one complete frame per layer, window capped at 8 MB, trailing bytes refused) (OWS-tolerant ordered chains; malformed/unsupported members fail closed). Each gzip/x-gzip layer must contain exactly one complete member with a valid trailer and no remaining bytes; additional members (even empty ones), padding, and trailing data fail closed with 400. The shared request representation gate applies the same rule; a claimed response representation rejects these forms with its existing 502 inspection error (gRPC INTERNAL). Unclaimed encoded responses retain their existing pass-through behavior. Null selects the default.
